concepts.name: Heat
concepts.statement: Energy that flows into or out of a system as heat, q; in the absence of other changes it would change the system's temperature.

concepts.name: Work
concepts.statement: Energy that flows as work, w: an infinitesimal displacement of the system multiplied by the force that resists it, integrated along the path the change follows.

concepts.name: Change in internal energy
concepts.statement: The change in internal energy between the initial and final states of a system, ΔU = U_f − U_i.

concepts.name: First law of thermodynamics
concepts.statement: The capacity of a system to do work is increased by heating the system or doing work on it: the change in its internal energy is the heat that flows in plus the work done on it, ΔU = q + w.

concepts.name: Endothermic and exothermic processes
concepts.statement: A process in which heat flows into the system is endothermic (q_system > 0); one in which heat flows out of the system is exothermic (q_system < 0).

concepts.name: Heat capacity
concepts.statement: The heat needed per unit rise in temperature, C = dq/dT, so that dq = C dT; it is usually given per mole, in J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.

concepts.name: State function
concepts.statement: A property of a system whose value depends only on the system's state, so that its change between two states is the same whatever path joins them; U and p are state variables.

concepts.name: Partial derivative
concepts.statement: The slope of a function of several variables with respect to one of them while the others are held fixed.

forms.latex: \left( \dfrac{ \partial f}{\partial x_i} \right)_{x_j \neq i} = \lim_{\Delta _i \rightarrow 0} \left( \dfrac{f(x_1+ \Delta x_1 , x_2 + \Delta x_2, \dots, x_i +\Delta x_i, \dots x_n+\Delta x_n) - f(x_1,x_2, \dots x_i, \dots x_n) }{\Delta x_i} \right)

concepts.name: Total differential
concepts.statement: An infinitesimal change in a function of several variables is the sum of its partial derivatives, each times the change in its own variable, so each contribution can be considered separately; for an ideal gas dp = (∂p/∂V)_T dV + (∂p/∂T)_V dT.

forms.latex: dp = \left( \dfrac{\partial p}{ \partial V} \right)_{T} dV + \left( \dfrac{\partial p}{ \partial T} \right)_{V} dT

concepts.name: Pressure is a state function
concepts.statement: The change in pressure of an ideal gas between two states comes out the same whether it goes by an isothermal step then an isochoric one or the other way round: pressure is a state variable, and its change does not depend on the pathway.

concepts.name: Kinds of work
concepts.statement: Work can be expansion against a resisting pressure, pushing charge through a circuit, extension against a tension or stretching a surface against a surface tension; each is an infinitesimal displacement times a resisting force.

concepts.name: Work as a line integral
concepts.statement: Work is the integral along the path of the inner product of a force and the path element, w = ∫F·ds.

concepts.name: Sign convention for heat and work
concepts.statement: Positive heat and positive work are energy put into the system; energy the system gives off as heat or work takes a minus sign.

concepts.name: External pressure
concepts.statement: The pressure the surroundings exert on the system, P_ext, as on the outside of a piston.

concepts.name: Pressure-volume work
concepts.statement: The work of a change of volume against a pressure, w_PV = −∫P dV in the sign convention; one form of work among others.

concepts.name: Work against a constant external pressure
concepts.statement: When the external pressure is constant, the work is w = −P_ext ΔV; if it changes along the way, w = −∫P_ext(V) dV.

concepts.name: Irreversible process
concepts.statement: A process in which the system's pressure differs from the pressure exerted on it, so the system passes through states out of equilibrium that cannot be drawn on a PV diagram; the forces balance only at the end.

concepts.name: Work as an area on a PV diagram
concepts.statement: The work of a volume change is the area under the external pressure on a PV diagram between the initial and final volumes, even where the process itself cannot be drawn.

concepts.name: Path function
concepts.statement: A quantity, such as work or heat, that depends on the path taken between two states; it is an energy transfer, not a property of the system.

concepts.name: Reversible process
concepts.statement: A path that follows a series of states at rest, the forces balanced at all times (P_ext = P), as in a compression in infinitesimally small steps.

concepts.name: Work of a reversible isothermal volume change
concepts.statement: For an ideal gas changed reversibly at constant temperature from V₁ to V₂, w = −nRT ln(V₂/V₁).

concepts.name: Reversible paths need least work and deliver most
concepts.statement: Between the same two states, the reversible isothermal path needs the least work to compress a gas and gets the most work out of its expansion; a one-step irreversible path needs more and delivers less.

concepts.name: Exact and inexact differentials
concepts.statement: A straight d marks the change of a state function (dU), a crooked δ the path-dependent amounts of heat and work (δq, δw); only ΔU = U₂ − U₁ follows from the end points alone.

concepts.name: Internal energy is a state function
concepts.statement: The internal energy is conserved: around any closed cycle its change is zero, ∮dU = 0, though heat and work can be produced, destroyed and turned into each other.

concepts.name: Isothermal change of an ideal gas leaves U unchanged
concepts.statement: The energy of an ideal gas depends only on its temperature, so in an isothermal change ΔU = 0 and the work and the heat cancel, w = −q.

concepts.name: Heat of a reversible isothermal expansion
concepts.statement: In a reversible isothermal expansion of an ideal gas the heat taken in is q_rev = nRT ln(V₂/V₁), positive when V₂ > V₁.

concepts.name: Adiabatic process
concepts.statement: A process in which no energy as heat crosses the system's boundary, δq = 0.

concepts.name: In an adiabatic process the energy change is the work
concepts.statement: With no heat flowing, dU = δw_rev: the work of an adiabatic expansion comes from the internal energy, so the temperature of the gas drops.

concepts.name: Energy change of an ideal gas from its heat capacity
concepts.statement: Since the energy of an ideal gas changes only with temperature, dU = C_V dT along any path; per mole dŪ = C̄_V dT.

concepts.name: Two reversible paths between the same states
concepts.statement: Going from P₁, V₁, T₁ to P₂, V₂, T₁ along the isotherm A or along the adiabat B and the isochore C gives the same ΔU = 0, but the heats and works differ: w_B = −q_C and w_A ≠ w_B, so work is a path function even when reversible.

forms.latex: \Delta U_{B+C} = \Delta U_A = 0 = q_B + w_B + q_C + w_C

concepts.name: Heat capacities of an ideal gas at constant pressure and volume
concepts.statement: For an ideal gas the molar heat capacities differ by the gas constant, C̄_P − C̄_V = R; for n moles C_p = C_V + nR.

concepts.name: Heat capacity ratio
concepts.statement: The ratio γ = C̄_P/C̄_V of the constant-pressure and constant-volume heat capacities; for an ideal gas R/C̄_V = γ − 1.

concepts.name: Temperature and volume in a reversible adiabatic change
concepts.statement: Along a reversible adiabatic path of an ideal gas, T₂/T₁ = (V̄₁/V̄₂)^(γ−1): as the volume increases the temperature decreases.

concepts.name: Molecular interpretation of heat and work
concepts.statement: A change in the energy of a system, dU = Σ ε_j dN_j + Σ N_j dε_j, has two parts: heat shifts the populations of fixed energy levels, and reversible work shifts the levels themselves while the populations stay put; the pressure follows from the partition function as P = kT(∂ln Q/∂V).

concepts.name: Enthalpy
concepts.statement: The state function H ≡ U + PV.

concepts.name: Differential of the enthalpy
concepts.statement: Under reversible conditions with no work other than pressure-volume work, dH = δq + V dP.

concepts.name: Heat at constant pressure is the enthalpy change
concepts.statement: With no other work, the heat taken in at constant pressure is the enthalpy change, ΔH = q_P, as the heat at constant volume is the energy change, ΔU = q_V.

concepts.name: Molar heat of fusion
concepts.statement: The heat needed at constant pressure to melt one mole of a solid, Δ_fus H = H_liquid − H_solid at the melting point.

concepts.name: Enthalpy and energy differ for gases
concepts.statement: Because the volume change is small, U ≈ H for condensed matter; the difference matters for gases.

concepts.name: Heat capacity is a path function
concepts.statement: The heat capacity depends on what is kept constant: at constant volume and at constant pressure it differs, little for most materials and by nR for an ideal gas.

concepts.name: Heat capacity at constant pressure
concepts.statement: The rate of change of the enthalpy with temperature at constant pressure, C_P = (∂H/∂T)_P.

concepts.name: Finding enthalpies from heat capacities
concepts.statement: Measuring C_p as a function of temperature and integrating it gives H(T), relative to a reference temperature, with the heat of each phase transition added where H jumps.

concepts.name: Heat capacity at a phase transition
concepts.statement: At a phase transition H jumps at a fixed temperature, so ΔH/ΔT is infinitely large and C_p has a singularity.

concepts.name: There are no absolute enthalpies
concepts.statement: Only differences in enthalpy, ΔH, are properly defined, and only for processes.

concepts.name: Adding enthalpy changes along a process
concepts.statement: Define the process, then add the enthalpy change of each step: heating each phase (∫C_P dT) and each transition, as ΔH_total = ΔH₁ + Δ_fus H + ΔH₃ for warming ice from −20 to +20 °C.

concepts.name: Differential scanning calorimetry
concepts.statement: Heating a sample pan and an empty reference pan at a constant rate, the small temperature difference between them measures the heat capacity of the sample against temperature; a melting shows as a broadened peak whose area is Δ_fus H.

concepts.name: Reaction enthalpy
concepts.statement: The enthalpy change Δ_rH of a reaction as written: doubling the equation doubles it, and the reverse reaction has the same enthalpy with the opposite sign.

concepts.name: Hess's law
concepts.statement: Because enthalpy is a state function, enthalpy changes of reactions are additive: the enthalpy of a reaction that is the sum of steps is the sum of their enthalpies, so it can be found even when the reaction is hard to carry out.

concepts.name: Standard state
concepts.statement: The most stable form of a substance at 1 atmosphere pressure and the specified temperature.

concepts.name: Standard formation reaction
concepts.statement: The reaction that forms one mole of a substance in its standard state from its elements in their standard states.

concepts.name: Standard enthalpy of formation
concepts.statement: The enthalpy of a standard formation reaction, ΔH_f°; for a pure element in its standard state it is zero, which sets the zero of the enthalpy scale.

concepts.name: Reaction enthalpy from enthalpies of formation
concepts.statement: A reaction enthalpy is the sum of the enthalpies of formation of the products less that of the reactants, each times its stoichiometric coefficient.

concepts.name: Electron affinity
concepts.statement: The first electron affinity is −ΔH(0 K) of X(g) + e⁻ → X⁻(g), defined with a minus sign so that most are positive; later electron affinities add further electrons.

concepts.name: Average bond enthalpy
concepts.statement: The enthalpy D(X–Y) of breaking a bond in the gas, XY(g) → X(g) + Y(g), averaged over many molecules that contain that bond.

concepts.name: Estimating a reaction enthalpy from bond enthalpies
concepts.statement: In the absence of formation enthalpies, ΔH_rxn ≈ Σ(bonds broken) − Σ(bonds formed), reliable to within about 5–10% since the bond enthalpies are averages for the gas phase.

concepts.name: Kirchhoff's law
concepts.statement: At constant pressure the enthalpy change over a temperature change is the integral of the heat capacity, ΔH = ∫C_p dT, which is C_pΔT when C_p is constant; for a reaction, ΔH_rxn(T₂) = ΔH_rxn(T₁) + ∫ΔC_p dT.

concepts.name: Empirical heat capacity model
concepts.statement: A common empirical fit of heat capacities over broad temperature ranges, C_p(T) = a + bT + c/T², with a, b and c found by experiment.

concepts.name: Enthalpy change from the empirical heat capacity
concepts.statement: Integrating a + bT + c/T² gives ΔH = a(T₂ − T₁) + (b/2)(T₂² − T₁²) − c(1/T₂ − 1/T₁).
